questions.question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains an error.

If she exercises daily, / she would / remain energetic / and fit forever.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1)**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the second part of the given sentence, the verb form 'would' is incorrect.
 
• The sentence structure suggests a conditional relationship.
 
• In conditional sentences, the present simple tense is used in the 'if' clause and the future simple tense is used in the main clause.
 
 
• Example: *If she** exercises** daily, she will remain energetic and fit forever.*
 
 
 
• Therefore, the correct form should be 'will' instead of 'would'.

Hence, the correct statement is: ***If she exercises daily, she will remain energetic and fit forever.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• If the **sentence is a conditional** statement, the correct structure is important.

 
 
• Example: *If it rains, we will stay indoors.*
 
 
 
• Use the **simple present tense** in the 'if' clause and the **simple future tense** in the main clause for most real conditional statements.
 
 
• Example: *If you study hard, you will pass the exam.*

questions.question:

A owl is a bird which has wide eyes, asymmetrical ears and is found mostly in forests.

options.text: and is found mostly in forests.

questions.solution:

__
 
• In the first part of the given sentence, the article 'A' is incorrect.
 
• In the given sentence, the correct article should be **'An'** because the noun **'owl'** begins with a vowel sound.
 
• Thus, the correct form should be **'An owl is a bird, which has wide eyes, asymmetrical ears and is found mostly in forests.'**

Hence, the correct statement is:** *An__ owl is a bird which has wide eyes, asymmetrical ears and is found mostly in forests*.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• When a noun starts with a vowel sound, the article 'An' is used before it.

 
 
• **Example:** ***An** apple a day keeps the doctor away.*
 
 
 
• When a noun starts with a consonant sound, the article 'A' is used before it.
 
 
• Example:** *****A **cat is sitting on the wall.*

questions.question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

The teacher will never / give you punishment / if you will / come on time.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** Option 1)**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the given sentence, the phrase 'if you will' is incorrect.
 
• In conditional sentences, the simple present tense is used in the **condition clause (after 'if').**
 
• The correct construction should be 'if you come'.
 
• **Example:** *If you come on time, the teacher will never give you punishment*.

Hence, the correct statement is: ***The teacher will never give you punishment if you come on time__*__.__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• In conditional sentences, when the condition clause (if-clause) is in the simple present tense, the result clause (main clause) is usually in the simple future tense.

 
 
• **Example:** *If it **rains**, we** will stay** indoors*.
 
 
 
• Do not use the future tense in the if-clause.
 
 
• Incorrect: *If you will come on time, we will start the meeting*.
 
• Correct: ***If you come on time, we will start the meeting*****.**

questions.question:

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution required’.

He asked his father when __would come the next letter__.
questions.solution:

__
 
• In the given sentence, **the verb phrase** should follow the correct word order for indirect questions.
 
• The correct structure for indirect questions is:** subject + verb.**
 
• Therefore, **"when would come the next letter"** should be corrected to "when the next letter would come".

Hence, the correct statement is: ***He asked his father when the next letter would come*.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• In direct questions, the structure is: question word + auxiliary verb + subject + main verb.
 
 
• **Example:** *When will the next letter come?*
 
 
 
• In indirect questions, the structure changes to: question word + subject + auxiliary verb + main verb.
 
 
• **Example:** *He asked when the next letter would come.*

If you do hard work, you will have the __expected results. __
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2)**

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The phrase "**desired results**" means the outcomes or results that one wants or wishes for.
 
• In the context of hard work, the results that one aims to achieve are typically the **"desired results."**
 
• The other options: "**required results**," "**good results**," and "**bad results**" do not appropriately convey the connotation of having goals or aspirations.

Therefore, the correct statement is: ***If you do hard work, you will have the desired results__.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Required results**: This implies results that are necessary, but not necessarily what one hopes for or desires.
 
• **Good results**: This is a general positive outcome but does not specify that it is what one aims for.
 
• **Bad results**: This is a negative outcome and opposite of what one would want from hard work.
